headline: Philippine Budget Deficit Widens to ₱161.3 Billion in August
seoTitle: Philippine Budget Deficit Widens to ₱161.3 Billion in August | FMB News
seoDescription: The Philippine government’s August 2026 budget deficit widened to ₱161.3 billion as spending rose 16% and revenue slipped 1.85%, Treasury data show.
deck: Treasury data show the monthly gap nearly doubled from a year earlier as spending rose to ₱507.3 billion and revenue eased to ₱346 billion; the eight-month deficit reached ₱1.05 trillion but remained within the ₱1.66-trillion full-year program.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Philippine national government recorded a ₱161.3-billion budget deficit in August 2026, up 90.23% from the ₱84.8-billion shortfall in August 2025, according to the Bureau of the Treasury.

The January-to-August deficit reached ₱1.0543 trillion, 21.3% wider than the ₱869.2-billion gap in the same period last year. Treasury said the cumulative shortfall remained within the government’s ₱1.66-trillion full-year deficit program.

sections.heading: What drove the wider gap
paragraphs: August revenue declined 1.85% year on year to ₱346 billion, largely because non-tax revenue fell 35.59%. Tax revenue still edged up 0.32% to ₱332.3 billion.

Government expenditure increased 16% to ₱507.3 billion. Treasury attributed much of the increase to ₱58.6 billion in budgetary support for PhilHealth premiums covering indigents, senior citizens and point-of-service patients, along with larger National Tax Allotment shares for local governments.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Interest payments reached ₱65.6 billion in August and ₱686.5 billion in the first eight months of 2026. The monthly primary deficit, which excludes interest payments, was ₱95.6 billion, according to Treasury’s cash-operations table.

A budget deficit means the government spent more than it collected during the period. It does not by itself establish fiscal distress; the size, financing cost, debt path and economic return of spending all matter.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: The figures affect how much the government must borrow and how much fiscal room remains for public services and investment. The data also show that the wider August gap was driven mainly by higher expenditure, including health-insurance support, while total monthly revenue declined modestly.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Future monthly cash-operations reports will show whether the deficit continues to track within the ₱1.66-trillion 2026 program and whether revenue growth, spending execution and interest costs change the year-end position.

verificationNotes: The Bureau of the Treasury’s official September 24 release reports an August deficit of ₱161.3 billion, up from ₱84.8 billion a year earlier, and an eight-month deficit of ₱1.0543 trillion within a ₱1.66-trillion full-year program.
The official cash-operations table reports August revenue of ₱346.0 billion and expenditure of ₱507.3 billion.
Philippine News Agency and The Philippine Star independently corroborate the headline figures, the ₱58.6-billion PhilHealth support and the main revenue and expenditure movements.
The article explains that a deficit is a period flow and does not alone establish fiscal distress.
